label: Squarish-shell 3BR / baths DISTRIBUTED, FRONT-BACK SPLIT with a rear corridor. The front half is master + great_room side by side; the whole rear band holds br2, br3, both baths and the kitchen, served by a corridor running across the band's front edge. br3's bath doors off the bedroom; the other bath doors off the corridor, which opens into the great_room.

adjacencies.note: great_room + kitchen form the open LDK (gr style), matching the source's continuous LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN volume

the east hall's mouth opens into the great_room. FIXED from the source: pep_SHD-2017036-DESIGN1 doors this connection off a single hinged door (flagged 'violated' against the rule 2 [PREFER] hallway-open-to-public default); this topology applies the catalog's standard open-mouth convention instead.
master (the source's largest, undesignated BEDROOM 1) doors into the east hall, at its front end
br2 doors into the east hall, at its rear end — matches the source's BEDROOM 2
east wing's shared bath doors into the hall, between master and br2 — matches the source's T&B between BEDROOM 2 and BEDROOM 1
geometry only, no door — matches the source's T&B/BEDROOM 1 shared wall
geometry only, no door — matches the source's BEDROOM 2/T&B shared wall

br3 doors directly onto the great_room — the half of the plan with NO dedicated hall, matching the source's BEDROOM 3 (which opens straight onto the open LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN volume with no hallway on that side of the plan at all). Kept as-is per rule 1's sanctioned tight-lot-bedroom-off-public exception, rather than forcing a hall this precedent never had.

br3's bath doors off the bedroom. In the half_spine parent this bath opened onto a vestibule (hall_w); removing that vestibule is what makes this topology feasible AND lets the bath reach its 3.0 m2 legal floor, which it never could with hall_w present at any lot size tested.

lot_adjustment_profiles.name: sq_front_back_split_baths_ds_hall_gr
lot_adjustment_profiles.rationale: The common_bath 3.0 m2 floor is the load-bearing entry and applies at every size this topology reaches, hence the deliberately generous threshold — without it the west bath settles around 2.0 m2, under the legal minimum. Caps on master/bedroom_standard and a hallway least-dimension floor were tried and are all individually infeasible here, so they are deliberately absent rather than forgotten.

notes: Squarish 3BR, baths distributed, front-back split with a rear corridor.
PROVENANCE — this is NOT a design drawn from a precedent. It is what
1s_3br_sq_half_spine_baths_ds_hall_gr actually resolves to once it is made
feasible, promoted to its own file under an honest name on 2026-08-13.
That parent (sourced from pep_SHD-2017036-DESIGN1) is infeasible at every
lot size as authored, and every route to fixing it either stays infeasible
or lands here. Keeping this under the half_spine name would have been the
'relabelled side_split' the parent's own notes warn against, so it was
separated instead. The parent is retained, unshipped, for a proper redraw.
WHAT IT IS. Front half: master (left) and great_room (right), side by side,
both full depth. Rear band: common_e, br2, common_w, br3 and kitchen across
the back. hall_e runs east-west along the front edge of that band and opens
into the great_room — a rear corridor, not a wing spine. master and br2 door
off it, common_e doors off it, and br3's bath (common_w) doors off br3.
WHAT CHANGED FROM THE PARENT. Three things, and the first is the one that
matters: hall_w (a bath vestibule) was REMOVED. It was wedged between br3 and
a great_room that also had to reach hall_e and the kitchen, so great_room
wrapped the west side and crushed it — br3 6.2 m2, common_w 2.0, hall_w 1.5,
against great 50.6 and master 32.2, with the kitchen down to 3.5. Removing it
recovers the kitchen to 7.0, br3 to 9.0, drops master to 24.9, and lets
common_bath reach its 3.0 m2 legal floor — which was unsatisfiable at EVERY
lot size with hall_w present, tested up to 20x16. Also: left_anchored and
right_anchored nulled (declared together they are infeasible — the
over-constrained-anchors trap), and zone_split nulled (the parent's was wrong
regardless: it declared private_side 'right' while listing only the east
rooms, though br3 and common_w are private and sit west).
VERIFIED 2026-08-13. Canonical 14x14: 90.0 m2 floor, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Typical split: great ~34-35, master ~25-26, bedrooms 6.0-7.5, kitchen 4.5-6.0, baths 3.0 and 4.5. Individual figures shift a little between runs (CP-SAT is non-deterministic even with a fixed seed); the totals and arrangement are stable.
Also solves 13.5x13.5 (80.8 m2, the band floor) and 15x15 (110.0). INFEASIBLE
at 13x13 and below. All inside the 80-120 m2 3BR/2-bath band.
KNOWN WEAKNESS: br2 sits at the 6.0 m2 hard floor while master takes 24.9, so
the bedroom hierarchy is lopsided. Caps on master_bedroom or bedroom_standard
are individually infeasible here, and set_max_area_sqm does not bite because
snap_gaps and the dead-strip claimer inflate rooms after the solve. Live with
it or re-tune; do not assume it is untried.
